verdict.rationale: React's first-party docs explicitly support incremental adoption. You can add React to an existing HTML page and render components anywhere on it. Multiple roots are supported for "sprinkles" of React on one page. You can move whole route subtrees to React, and the docs point to full-stack frameworks like Next.js when you want to build an entire app. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the migration path from a partial page to a full app, since all evidence is first-party.

support.subject: As a developer, I can incrementally adopt the framework, scaling from a small part of a page up to a full application

citations.quote: You don’t have to build your whole page in React. Add React to your existing HTML page, and render interactive React components anywhere on it.
A page that uses "sprinkles" of React for parts of the page may have as many separate roots as needed.
you want to implement all routes starting with `example.com/some-app/` fully with React.
To build an entire app with React, we recommend a full-stack React framework like Next.js or React Router.
you can use as little or as much React as you need
